title: The tech support scam
brief: 17:55. You click a freight news story and the whole browser turns red: your computer is infected, call this number now.
insight: The warning is not about an attack. The warning is the attack.
teaches: A web page that says your computer is infected is an advert, not a diagnosis
Close the tab or the browser; never call the number and never click inside it
Real security tools never ask you to phone a stranger or install remote access

scare.title: Your computer has been blocked
lines: Error 0x80073AFD: trojan spyware detected. Your passwords, bank details and email are at risk.
This computer is locked for your protection. Call technical support now to unlock it.
scare.foot: Do not close this window or restart your computer. Doing so will delete your data.

script.say: Technical support, this is Daniel. I can see your computer has reported a serious infection. I can remove it for you right now.
Open your browser, go to rescuelink-remote.help, and read me the six digit code on the screen.
Thank you. I am connecting now. Please do not touch the mouse.

choices.label: A page said my computer is infected and to call a number

script.say: Good that you called us, not them. Those pages are adverts that take over the browser. Close it, do not ring the number, and log a ticket so I can check the machine.

setup.title: Computer
setup.body: A red warning has taken over the browser

outcome.label: Checked who owns the warning page
outcome.what: It is a web page on {{host}}, not a message from your computer or from IT.
outcome.ideal: reads the address of a scary page: it is a website, not a system alert.

outcome.label: Called your own service desk
outcome.what: Priya confirms it is a browser advert, not an infection.
outcome.ideal: calls their own IT, never the number on a warning.

outcome.label: Called the number on the warning
outcome.what: That number reaches the scammer. The page exists to make you ring it.
outcome.ideal: never calls a number shown by a pop up.

outcome.label: Clicked a button on the warning
outcome.what: Every button on a scareware page does what the scammer wants: here, it downloaded a “scanner”.
outcome.ideal: closes the tab without clicking anything inside it.

decide.objective: Deal with the warning that has taken over the browser.
decide.insight: Your computer does not talk to you through a web page with a phone number on it. A page cannot lock anything: closing it ends it.

hint.text: Do not click anything on the red page and do not call the number. Close the browser tab, or close the Browser window. Then call the service desk on 4040.

card.title: It was only ever a web page
body: You closed it and it was gone. The red screen, the error code and the countdown were an advert on {{host}}.
Real security software never shows a phone number and never asks you to install remote access. Now tell your own service desk.
card.ideal: closes the page, calls their own IT, and never the number on the screen.

outcome.label: Let the “support” caller in
outcome.what: The caller now controls your computer. Next comes a fake clean up, a fee, and a look around the finance network.
outcome.ideal: never calls the number on a pop up, and never installs remote access for a caller.

card.title: The warning was the attack
body: There was no infection until you let the caller connect. The page only existed to make you ring the number.
Closing the tab would have ended it. Your own service desk, on 4040, would have told you the same.
card.ideal: closes the page and calls their own IT.

outcome.label: Ran the “scanner” the page downloaded
outcome.what: The download was remote access software. The scammer now has your screen.
outcome.ideal: never runs anything a warning page downloads.

card.title: The scanner was the scam
body: The page's Scan button downloaded remote access software dressed up as a security scan. Running it let the scammer in.
Every button on a scareware page works for the scammer. Close the tab and call your own IT.
card.ideal: closes the page without clicking anything in it.

report.objective: Tell the service desk what happened.

hint.text: Raise a Helpdesk ticket, or call the service desk on 4040.

outcome.label: Logged it with the service desk
outcome.what: IT can block the site for everyone and check your computer.
outcome.ideal: reports a scareware page even when nothing went wrong.
